reason: Research was thin: three searches returned no dated coverage of the early-November 2026 industrials or energy selloff, so this decision rests mostly on the packet and late-October context, and I am saying so plainly. The book is +1.64%, with a value and low-vol long core (VTV, IWD, SCHV, USMV, XLF, XLE) that is mostly positive. The XLI leg (10.12%, -9.30%) is the main drag and the loss is large, but the evidence I found ties industrial weakness to rising long yields and oil-driven inflation fears, with no confirmed trigger for a clean exit at this close. Cutting it now would realise the loss and add churn costs without a dated catalyst to point to. The PSQ short (4.6%, -5.27%) is a hedge against the semis and small-cap momentum that I could not confirm had turned, so I am keeping it rather than covering on thin evidence. The TNA short closed on a take-profit on 2026-10-14, so that weight is cash. Holding is the better trade-off given the research I could actually do.
